copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Spain v Cabo Verde in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Monday, and the model and the market disagree on the the draw side by +3.1pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Elo numbers going in: Spain 2010, Cabo Verde 1540. That's a 470-point lead for Spain — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Spain to win at 84%, the draw at 10%, and Cabo Verde to win at 6%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. the draw on the win side reads 10%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Spain to win at 89%, the draw at 7%, and Cabo Verde to win at 4%. Polymarket has the draw at 7%, which prices out at American odds of +1349; the model has the same side at 10%. The +3.1pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On the draw, that haircut lands the model at 10%; the market is at 7%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +3.1pp. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the the draw side specifically.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 24 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
Bootstrap lower-bound on the the draw side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives the draw a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
